site.name: Melanie Cleary
site.description: Melanie Cleary is a Creative Director with an art direction background, based in New York City. This site is a collection of her work.

body: I’m Mel, a Creative Director with an art direction background living and working in New York City. I graduated with a BFA in Visual Communications from the University of Delaware in 2014.
In my free time I’m either doodling houses, working my way through all of the Oscar nominated movies, making soup, or reading a book.

html: To launch Walmart’s new Rx Express Delivery service, we took a page out of the most iconic sick day in movie history, Ferris Bueller’s Day Off — giving Walmart’s newest delivery offering the Hollywood treatment. We tapped Anna Faris to bring the humor, connect with our audience, and give a familiar movie (and a conveniently similar name) a new spin.
The result was an ode to staying home, doing absolutely nothing, and letting Walmart handle the rest. Ferris would be proud.

And audiences were into it. The campaign outperformed historical brand benchmarks, with over 50% of viewers watching the full 60-second spot. It was also ranked the #9 most recalled ad in the US in Q3 2025 by Cubery.
And for anyone paying close attention, we snuck in some Easter eggs from the original movie. Bueller? Bueller? How many can you spot?

Coming off the launch of Walmart’s Who Knew? campaign, people were starting to realize just how much Walmart has to offer. But there was another side of Walmart we wanted them to get to know too… the wellness side. From Rx delivery and sea moss to flu shots and glasses, Walmart had a lot more going on than people might expect.
Because just like the people who shop there, Walmart is multifaceted. So we leaned into the duality of our customers (and Walmart itself) to show that there’s more to everyone than meets the eye.

Enter our cast of characters: Benji, our punk-rock doggy daddy who’s also a chill yogi and green smoothie sipper. Meema, our crochet champ who doubles as a boot-scootin’ baddie. And Vicky, our avid reader who also knows how to paint the town red.
Three very different personalities, each with more than one side. A little reminder that whatever side of yourself you’re leaning into today, Walmart has something for that, too.

We kept the dual personalities going on social, tapping creator Kristen Marie to do what she does best: lean into the different personalities she portrays in her content, each with their own wellness needs… and quirks.
Walmart is a big supporter of American businesses. In fact, most of what Walmart spends on products goes toward things made, grown, or assembled right here in the U.S. Who knew?

As part of Walmart’s Who Knew? campaign, we wanted to put some real faces (and stories) behind that stat. So we teamed up with Fire Department Coffee, a veteran-owned, firefighter-run coffee company that went from Walmart’s Open Call to shelves nationwide.

We put the company’s two real-life founders in front of the camera for their commercial debut, letting them tell their story in their own words. From what Walmart’s support has meant for their growing business to what that growth has allowed them to give back to their community, we showed how supporting American businesses can have an impact well beyond the store shelves.

What happens when America’s favorite chocolate chip cookie decides it’s time for an upgrade? A journey of self-improvement — or as we called it, MMMprovement — to become even more delicious. And who better to help get the word out than the queen of self-improvement (and hilarious interviews) herself, Keke Palmer.

We created a campaign that gave our recipe the full media run, PR treatment, with Chip as our charismatic star, and Keke Palmer in the role she was born to play: a talk show host. Starting with :15s that ran on CTV and socials, we also blew it out with brand content and two paid social videos on Keke’s pages, visually fitting right in with her beloved content.
In a world… where Braces are Drama, Invisalign is the drama free option to straighten your teeth.

To highlight all of the ways braces are drama we turned to the most dramatic medium of all: MOVIES. We created what looked like trailers for upcoming new releases but the plot of every movie was centered around the drama of braces. With trailers for 8 totally different genres of movies we created something for every teen on the internet — from a disaster movie to a movie musical.

We paired our trailers with animated movie posters tailored for social placements and worked with creators on TikTok to create their own movie trailers, tapping into a behavior that was already gaining traction on social platforms.
And the trailers found their audience with tangible results: 127% increase in views from our target, 315% increase in clickthrough rate and 404k unique website visits from teens.

html: Our trailer for the fictional flick, Vampires in Wires, premiered in a Vevo Takeover on YouTube for Olivia Rodrigo’s hit song of the summer, “vampire.” And our trailer for the fictional action flick Down to the Wire premiered on TikTok around the launch of Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning to integrate Invisalign into pre-existing cultural conversations.
We cut our trailers into :06s, :15s and :30s for different media placements.
A new 360º campaign for belVita Breakfast Biscuits with an aim to bring humor into the breakfast space while also letting consumers in on what a breakfast biscuit actually is.
In addition to our TVC and digital :15 and :30 we created assets specifically for social — including an asset that hacked the IG/Facebook “Collection” unit.

Heavy-hitting benefit and product focused assets were created with CG and 3D for both YouTube and social to help consumers have a better understanding of belVita, since breakfast biscuits aren’t too common in the US.

For Mental Health Awareness month in 2022 Trident was proud to assist NBA player Trae Young and his foundation, Trae Young Family Foundation (TYFF), in their mission to support all people and their mental health.

The content was shared on social by both Trident and Trae Young. Additionally, a suite of assets were created for in-store viewing in Walmarts around the country that were selling limited edition TYFF Trident packs.
“Out of Bounds” and “Pause” are assets created with social habits in mind — designed to hack the feed and interrupt people’s endless scrolling.
2019 was American Express’ first year as an official sponsor of The Championships, Wimbledon.

Featuring 3-time Grand Slam Winner, Andy Murray and a real grass arm chair + footrest: this content was created to promote on-site offers and celebrate the brand new partnership on both US and UK channels.
A content series to promote Small Business Saturday with Shaq leading the charge.
We captured him in real small businesses across the US with his friends Kendrick Lamar, Jeremy Piven, and Wanda Sykes.
We leveraged our footage to create GIFs for social and online placements.
A new TVC campaign aimed to make all coffee-drinkers also biscuit-eaters.
A 360 campaign ranging from pre-roll and media partnerships to social content and a photo library for the American Express product Pay It Plan It.

html: A sampling from our Pay It Plan It photo library:

We all know those special moments we experience in small businesses: when someone knows your “usual,” the guy you never talk to but give a nod to every Friday at the local pub, the corner booth at your fave place. We sought to recreate those moments and captured them in real small businesses around New York City to get people excited to go out and Shop Small on Small Business Saturday.
Our content ran as pre-roll and social — both general and hyper-targeted.
Our geo-targeted social ads populated with timely data based on favorite small businesses in the targeted location and trending interests in those areas.
